01.event: The freed sons of Yudan the maidservant are permitted to marry each other's wives
01.turn: Rava objects that Rav Sheshet prohibited it
01.outcome: Rav Aha says: he prohibited and I permit
01.summary: The sons of Yudan the maidservant were freed, and Rav Aha bar Ya'akov permitted them to marry each other's wives. Rava objected that Rav Sheshet had prohibited this; Rav Aha replied that he disagrees.
01.missing: Any action or change beyond the ruling and the scholarly exchange
01.reason: One background event (the freeing) followed by a ruling and an ordinary scholarly disagreement; nothing changes afterwards, so under R-C0's 2026-10-25 limit it is not a story.

02.event: A marriage contract with a recognized scribe's hand and one witness is brought before him
02.turn: He thinks to validate it; Rabbi Yirmeya corrects him
02.summary: A marriage contract was brought before Rabbi Abbahu, and he thought to validate it on the scribe's handwriting and one witness. Rabbi Yirmeya told him the mishna requires the scribe to have signed.
02.missing: Any event beyond the case being brought and the legal exchange
02.reason: A case before a rabbi where coming before him is the only event, followed by legal discussion; no change is narrated.

03.missing: Any event: it is a question, an answer, and testimony about past families
03.reason: A question and answer with a testimony cited as legal evidence; speech with no event and no real conflict.

04.event: Visits his son-in-law Rav Hisda and places his great-granddaughter on his lap
04.turn: Rav Hisda questions it; they trade accusations of violating Rav's and Shmuel's rulings
04.outcome: Rav Aha justifies himself by another statement of Shmuel
04.summary: Rav Aha bar Abba visited his son-in-law Rav Hisda and took his granddaughter's daughter on his lap. Rav Hisda challenged him, and the two traded charges of having transgressed rulings of Rav and Shmuel, until Rav Aha cited Shmuel's 'all for the sake of Heaven'.
04.reason: There is a real event (the visit and the act) but the passage is mainly a pointed dialogue; mainly speech with something happening is borderline.

05.actor: Rav Yehezkel and his son Rav Yehuda
05.event: Rav Yehezkel teaches a mishna to his son Rami
05.turn: His other son Rav Yehuda tells him not to teach it that way and they argue
05.outcome: Shmuel rebukes Rav Yehuda for speaking so to his father
05.summary: Rav Yehezkel was teaching his son Rami, and his other son Rav Yehuda told him not to teach the mishna that way, arguing the point with him. Later Shmuel rebuked Rav Yehuda for addressing his father so disrespectfully.
05.missing: Any action beyond speech; the dispute is a textual argument
05.reason: Teaching and arguing are speech, but there is a conflict (a son contradicting his father) and a rebuke that follows; mainly speech with conflict is borderline.

06.missing: Any narrated event; it is a resolution of contradictory statements
06.reason: The Gemara resolves a contradiction by dating Rav's statements; no event is narrated.

07.missing: A one-time event or consequence; only habitual practices are reported
07.reason: A ruling followed by reports of what Rabbi Yohanan and Rava used to do; a custom that leads nowhere is not a story.

08.missing: Anything beyond a precedent cited as evidence and its legal analysis
08.reason: A bare report of a collection on promissory notes, cited as proof and then analysed; no one responds and nothing follows.

09.event: A heretic mocks him as a 'man of thorns' citing Micah
09.turn: He retorts, calling the heretic a fool and reinterpreting the verse
09.outcome: The verse is turned into praise
09.summary: A heretic insulted Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hananya, calling Israel's best mere thorns. Rabbi Yehoshua called him a fool and read the verse as praise.
09.missing: Any event beyond the exchange of words
09.reason: Speech alone, but with genuine conflict (a heretic's mockery and a retort); under R-C2 that is borderline.

10.missing: Any action or change beyond the betrothal that triggers the legal dispute
10.reason: One event (betrothal with silk) followed only by an amoraic dispute and its analysis; not a story.

11.actor: A man in Rabbi Ami's neighbourhood
11.event: Rabbi Ami declares him a mamzer
11.outcome: Rabbi Ami tells him he has given him life
11.summary: Rabbi Ami publicly declared a neighbour to be a mamzer. The man went about weeping, until Rabbi Ami told him that by the declaration he had given him life.
11.reason: A declaration, an emotional reaction (which counts as an event) and a response that reframes it: more than one action and a change.

12.turn: Rabbi sends a pair of Sages; women tell them their husbands are coming
12.outcome: They retort 'let them be your husbands'
12.summary: The daughters-in-law of Abdan rebelled against their husbands, and Rabbi sent two Sages to examine them. When women told them their husbands were coming, they answered: let them be your husbands.
12.reason: Several narrated actions (rebellion, sending of Sages, the defiant reply) with conflict and change, cited as precedent but told as an incident.

13.event: He throws lentil bread to his dog
13.turn: The dog will not eat it
13.outcome: Cited as evidence that the bread is inedible
13.summary: In Mar Shmuel's days there was a lentil bread; he threw it to his dog and the dog would not eat it.
13.missing: Any human response or development; it is a one-line report cited as evidence
13.reason: Two events with a small result, but told only as evidence in a legal argument with little change; between borderline and not, so borderline.

14.event: An incident in which she removed her husband from his grave
14.summary: The Rabbis cite the incident of a woman who removed her husband from his grave; the details come only from the commentary.
14.missing: The incident itself; it is only alluded to
14.reason: An incident only alluded to, which must be filled in from the commentaries, is borderline under R-C6.

15.missing: Any one-time event; it reports a habitual way of speaking
15.reason: A habitual speech pattern with no event following; a custom that leads nowhere is not a story.

16.event: Rav Kahana asks him to recall testimony; he does not remember
16.turn: He eventually remembers and testifies; Rav Kahana hesitates
16.outcome: Rav Ashi tells him he remembered by his own effort, not relying on him
16.summary: Rav Kahana asked Rav Ashi whether he remembered some testimony, and Rav Ashi said he did not. Eventually Rav Ashi remembered and testified, and seeing Rav Kahana hesitate, assured him he had recalled it himself.
16.reason: Multiple actions (asking, remembering, testifying, hesitating) with a change from forgetting to remembering; an incident with a resolution.

17.event: A woman of Mehoza married to a man of Neharde'a comes before him
17.turn: He hears her accent and rules by Rav; they tell him she married into Neharde'a
17.outcome: He reverses and rules by Shmuel
17.summary: A woman from Mehoza married to a man from Neharde'a came before Rav Nahman. Recognising her accent he ruled according to Babylonian custom, but when told her husband was from Neharde'a he changed his ruling.
17.missing: Any action beyond the court hearing and the change of ruling
17.reason: A case before a rabbi, but the rabbi perceives something and changes his ruling, which is a little more than a ruling; borderline rather than not.

18.actor: Rav Pappa and Yehuda bar Mareimar
18.event: Rav Pappa goes to write his son's bride's ketubah; Yehuda bar Mareimar comes out to greet him
18.turn: At the entrance Yehuda takes his leave
18.outcome: Rav Pappa invites him in (continues past the passage)
18.summary: Rav Pappa went to supervise the ketubah for his son's marriage into Abba of Sura's family. Yehuda bar Mareimar came out to greet him but took his leave at the door, and Rav Pappa asked him to come in.
18.missing: The resolution, which lies in the following segments
18.reason: Several narrated actions with a tension that begins to turn; the passage is the opening of a story, so it contains a story.

19.missing: Any action beyond the instruction in the will and a ruling
19.reason: One instruction and a price change, then a ruling; nothing else happens, so it is not a story.

20.event: A case of an alleyway ending in a backyard comes before him
20.outcome: He requires nothing to permit carrying
20.summary: An incident in a shepherds' village came before Rav Yehuda, and he did not require anything to permit the alleyway. Rav Yosef cites it in legal discussion.
20.missing: Any event beyond the case reaching the rabbi and his ruling
20.reason: Coming before a rabbi is the only event and the ruling follows; under R-C0's limit it is not a story.
